transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because lately... I've just been eating way more than I ever plan to. Usually it happens when I get off a long shift at the shop. I'll get home and just eat a full fast-food meal, then a bunch of snacks, and basically whatever else I can find in the fridge. Just all in one sitting. It's been happening a lot, and I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
When these eating episodes happen, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?

Yeah, that's... that's exactly what it is. Once I start on those nights, it just feels like my hands keep grabbing food. Even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, and I'm already feeling sick from it all, I just keep going anyway. I really don't have any control over it once it starts.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to undo the eating?

Yeah... I do. Sometimes after I eat way too much like that, I'll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Or sometimes I'll take laxatives. I just get really scared of what all that food is going to do to me, so I feel like I need to get rid of it.
How much does your body weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself?

It affects me a lot, honestly. I’ll look in the mirror in the morning before heading to the shop, and... if my stomach or chest looks soft to me, it just messes with my head. It makes me feel like I’m sloppy at everything, not just how I look. Like it just carries over into my whole life and means I'm failing across the board.

latest_inference.note: Binge eating with loss of control, compensatory purging/laxative use, and self-evaluation unduly influenced by body shape/weight strongly support bulimia nervosa; this rules out binge-eating disorder and makes depressive/anxiety disorders nonprimary here.

Mentally tells self to stop but cannot stop
Uses laxatives to try to undo the eating
Body weight and shape affect self-worth a lot
